segments.text: Stylus Hook. Uniswap v4 hooks written entirely in Rust, on Arbitrum Stylus.

It started at Scaling Ethereum, 2024, and won the Arbitrum Stylus track. But the contract Uniswap actually called was Solidity: a proxy, forwarding every callback to our Stylus code behind it. The logic was Rust. The hook was not.
Two things forced that, and neither was the idea. Uniswap v4 was still being built. And Stylus was not on mainnet yet.
Both have shipped since. Version four is live. Stylus is on mainnet. And cargo stylus now deploys through a CREATE2 deployer.
Uniswap asks a hook for two things. Answer the IHooks interface, which Stylus gets free. And live at an address whose low fourteen bits encode its callbacks. The address was the blocker.
So, three pieces. A Stylus port of BaseHook, with all ten callbacks. A macro for the safety guards. And a miner for the CREATE2 salt. No Solidity left anywhere.
Five steps. Storage, permissions, validate the mined address, implement the callbacks, then mine the salt and deploy.
And the receipt: a real pool manager, on a real node, driving every callback of a Rust hook.
Is it worth it? Stylus is not faster. It is differently priced. Entering costs eight thousand gas more. Storage is identical. Arithmetic is three to six hundred times cheaper.
Same loop in both languages: they cross at eighty nine operations.
So most hooks should stay in Solidity. A hook that only keeps books costs three times more in Rust. Anything resting on a precompile gains nothing.
When it does pay, this is why. The E V M pays for a full two hundred and fifty six bit word whether the work needs one or not.
Now the case that matters, against the TWAMM live on Base and Unichain. Long term orders are placed independently, so several running at once is the ordinary state of a busy pool.
And that is the argument. The entry fee is paid once per swap. The saving, once per stream. At thirty two concurrent orders: Solidity, two point eight five million gas. Rust, one point eight nine.
And one thing Solidity cannot do at all. SHAKE is not behind the E V M's Keccak opcode. One post quantum signature check: eleven million gas in Solidity, thirty three thousand in Rust.
Two traps cost an order of magnitude each. An optimisation level that fails only at deployment, and constants built from strings.
Porting is the harshest way to read a protocol. We found a failing input in v4 core's own tick math fuzz test. The fix is one character.
All open source. If you want to write a Uniswap v4 hook in Rust, the hard parts are done.
